references.text: The parallel account in Matthew where a scribe says to Jesus that he will follow him wherever he goes, and Jesus answers with the words that the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head. This is the closest parallel to Luke 9:57.
Elisha left everything and followed Elijah after Elijah cast his cloak over him. This is an Old Testament type of following a prophet or master, which is the theme in Jesus' call to discipleship.
Jesus speaks about what it costs to follow him: to deny oneself and take up one's cross daily. The man who says he will follow Jesus 'wherever you go' is here confronted with exactly this cost.
Jesus teaches about counting the cost of being his disciple. The man's spontaneous promise to follow Jesus everywhere thematically belongs with this teaching on the price of discipleship.
Ruth says to Naomi: 'Where you go, I will go.' Ruth's words recall the man's promise to Jesus to follow him wherever he goes and express a similar total devotion.
